answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks whose results are independently checked and whose payment comes from a bonded stake. A new identity must lock capital before it can influence decisions; if its work fails verification, the bond is slashed, while passing work earns reputation gradually. This makes a swarm of disposable accounts costly: each needs its own stake and verified history, and splitting one agent’s funds across cedar, ocean, and echo identities does not multiply the underlying capital.
